stories.headline: Appeals court increases Yoon Suk-yeol's obstruction sentence to 7 years; wife Kim Keon-hee's corruption sentence raised to 4 years
stories.summary: Seoul High Court on April 29 increased former President Yoon Suk-yeol's prison term from five to seven years for obstructing justice and bypassing a Cabinet meeting before his December 2024 martial law declaration; the court also found him guilty of additional charges. In a separate ruling on April 28, the same court raised ex-first lady Kim Keon-hee's sentence to four years on stock manipulation and bribery charges. A preliminary hearing in Yoon's insurrection appeal (life sentence) was also held on April 27, and a new special prosecutor team summoned Yoon for questioning.

stories.headline: Samsung posts record Q1 earnings on AI memory boom, warns supply shortage will worsen through 2027
stories.summary: Samsung Electronics reported an approximately eightfold increase in first-quarter 2026 operating profit to 57.3 trillion won, driven almost entirely by its chip division amid surging AI infrastructure demand. In the same earnings call the company warned of a severe memory supply shortage expected to deepen into 2027, with SK Hynix issuing similar warnings; the results also raised concerns about K-shaped economic divergence as chipmaker workers face record bonuses.

stories.headline: Lee Jae-myung calls for 'mutual respect' in US-Korea relations as alliance tensions mount
stories.summary: President Lee Jae-myung made a series of statements in late April and early May calling for resolution of pending issues with traditional allies — widely read as addressing US pressure over intelligence-sharing, defense autonomy, and regulation of American firms — on the basis of 'mutual respect, common sense and principles.' Lee also convened a luncheon with minor party and independent lawmakers on April 29 to urge bipartisan unity on foreign and security affairs, implicitly criticizing PPP leader Jang Dong-hyuk's recent Washington visit as 'self-defeating.'

stories.headline: KBank partners with Ripple to test blockchain-based cross-border remittances
stories.summary: South Korea's internet-only KBank, exclusive banking partner of crypto exchange Upbit, signed a strategic partnership with Ripple on April 27 to test blockchain-based overseas remittances using Ripple's Palisade wallet infrastructure. The proof-of-concept is underway in two phases targeting UAE and Thailand corridors, with a second phase linking KBank customer accounts; the deal comes as South Korea finalizes its Digital Asset Basic Act.

stories.headline: Bank of Korea holds rates steady at 2.50%, cites Iran war uncertainty; new governor outlines CBDC priorities
stories.summary: Minutes released April 28 from the Bank of Korea's April 10 meeting show the monetary policy board adopted a cautious wait-and-see stance, citing heightened uncertainty from the Iran war's impact on growth and inflation; the BOK kept its benchmark rate at 2.50%. Separately, new BOK Governor Shin Hyun-song, who will chair his first policy meeting May 28, outlined priorities including CBDCs and deposit tokens to globalize the won.

stories.headline: Lee Jae-myung delivers Labor Day workplace safety pledges; warns against excessive union demands ahead of Samsung strike threat
stories.summary: President Lee Jae-myung held the first Blue House Labor Day ceremony on May 2, pledging zero compromise on workplace safety and calling workers 'the backbone of the economy.' On April 28 he made similar remarks on Industrial Accident Workers Day. Later in the week Lee warned that excessive union demands could harm fellow workers — remarks interpreted as directed at Samsung Electronics' union, which threatened an 18-day strike from May 21 over bonus structures.

stories.headline: June 3 local elections and parliamentary by-elections heat up; PPP leadership divided, DPK aides resign to run
stories.summary: Preparations for the June 3 local elections and parliamentary by-elections intensified this week. Two senior presidential aides — AI secretary Ha Jung-woo and spokesperson Jeon Eun-soo — resigned to pursue DPK candidacies. PPP chairman Jang Dong-hyuk and floor leader Song Eon-seok are campaigning separately, raising concern about internal discord; PPP's Daegu chief apologized over nomination controversies. A DPK Busan candidate faced backlash over a viral 'hand-wiping' video. The K-Arts university relocation also became a campaign flashpoint.

stories.headline: North Korea naming controversy: Unification Ministry proposes using Pyongyang's preferred term 'Joseon'; PPP pushes back, opposition seeks minister's dismissal
stories.summary: The Guardian reported on a long-running South Korean debate over what to call North Korea, brought to the fore by the Unification Ministry's proposal to use North Korea's preferred name 'Joseon.' A senior PPP official publicly denounced the idea as unconstitutional and tantamount to recognizing a two-state theory; separately, PPP lawmakers called for a dismissal vote against Unification Minister Chung Dong-young, though DPK lawmakers walked out of the plenary session.

stories.headline: Korean banking sector pushes into digital finance: won-backed stablecoin, mobile ID expansion, and KB Financial's blockchain partnership
stories.summary: Several South Korean financial institutions announced digital finance moves this week: MoonPay Korea signed an MOU with Woori Bank to support global distribution of a won-backed stablecoin; KB Financial Group partnered with Pantera Capital for blockchain development and signed a separate MOU with the BOK for Project Han River (digital currency infrastructure testing); and the government announced expansion of its mobile ID service to 12 apps by 2027.

stories.headline: 96 South Korean lawmakers protest US congressional intervention in Coupang investigation
stories.summary: Representative Park Hong-bae and 95 other lawmakers from the DPK and allied minor parties held a press conference on April 28 to deliver a joint protest letter to the US over alleged attempts by US lawmakers to link the Korea-US alliance to a domestic investigation of Coupang, calling it an 'infringement on judicial sovereignty.'

stories.summary: A Realmeter poll released April 27 found President Lee's approval rating at 62.2%, down 3.3 percentage points from the prior week, attributed to economic concerns including ripple effects from the Iran war. The Democratic Party of Korea polled at 51.3% and the PPP at 30.7%.

stories.headline: Korean national appointed World Bank market risk director; Eximbank signs ADB minerals MOU
stories.summary: Min Jin-ah, a Korean banking veteran working at the World Bank's MIGA unit, was appointed Director for Market and Counterparty Risk at the World Bank Group — the fourth Korean to reach director level there. Separately, the Export-Import Bank of Korea signed an MOU with the Asian Development Bank to jointly finance critical minerals projects and stabilize supply chains for Korean companies.

stories.headline: ASEAN+3 and Korea-China-Japan finance ministers meet in Samarkand to strengthen regional safety net
stories.summary: Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Koo Yun-cheol attended ASEAN+3 Finance Ministers' meetings and an Asian Development Bank annual meeting in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, on May 3, where finance leaders accelerated efforts to strengthen a regional financial safety net amid Middle East war risks.

stories.summary: The People Power Party on April 28 accused MBC of broadcasting politically biased commentary — a closing remark by anchor Chu Kyung-ho about the insurrection trial — and threatened to refuse MBC coverage unless the broadcaster apologized, claiming 'election interference.'

stories.headline: South Korea launches next-generation earth observation satellite No. 2 on SpaceX Falcon 9
stories.summary: South Korea launched its next-generation mid-sized Earth observation satellite No. 2 aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on May 3, with development led by Korea Aerospace Industries to support land management, disaster response, and private-sector space technology.

articles.title: South Korea launches next-generation satellite on SpaceX Falcon 9, Yonhap says

stories.headline: Bell and KAI sign MoU to propose MV-75 tiltrotor for South Korea's helicopter replacement program
stories.summary: Bell Textron and Korea Aerospace Industries signed a memorandum of understanding on April 28 to study an MV-75 Cheyenne II tiltrotor solution for South Korea's HSMUH program, which seeks to replace approximately 103 Sikorsky UH-60P Black Hawks in ROK Army service.

articles.title: Bell, KAI sign MoU to pitch MV-75 tiltrotor for South Korea

stories.headline: South Korea commissions fourth Chungnam-class frigate, expects six domestically-built frigates by 2028
stories.summary: The Republic of Korea Navy commissioned the ROKS Jeju (FFG-832), its fourth Chungnam-class frigate, with two more planned before 2028; the frigates are built by Hyundai Heavy Industries and represent South Korea's continued investment in domestically produced blue-water naval vessels.

stories.headline: Daejang-dong corruption detainees released; figures implicate President Lee Jae-myung
stories.summary: Detention periods expired for three key Daejang-dong land development scandal figures — Yoo Dong-gyu, Nam Wook, and Kim Man-bae — who were released; Yoo was reported to have claimed that President Lee had prior knowledge of the corruption in the case.

stories.headline: Bank of Korea data shows AI is sharply reducing youth employment in exposed industries
stories.summary: A Seoul Economic Daily report citing Bank of Korea analysis of National Pension Service data found that youth employment in South Korea fell by 211,000 over three years, with 208,000 of those losses occurring in AI-exposed industries; the BOK noted AI more easily replaces routine tasks of younger, less-experienced workers.

stories.headline: Samsung family completes payment of record 12 trillion won inheritance tax over five years
stories.summary: The heirs of late Samsung chairman Lee Kun-hee, including Chairman Lee Jae-yong, completed payment of the 12 trillion won inheritance tax on his estate — one of the largest inheritance tax bills ever recorded globally — five years after his death in 2020.

articles.title: A World-First 12 Trillion Won Inheritance Tax: Samsung Family Finally Pays It Off After Five Years
